__title: Finta — Offline Budget & Expense Tracker, No Account
__desc: A personal finance tracker that runs entirely on your phone. No account, no cloud, no tracking — with budgets that reset on payday instead of the 1st.
__ogalt: Finta — your money stays on your phone. No account, no cloud, no tracking.

the_budget_tracker_that: The budget tracker that stays on your phone.
finta_is_a_personal: Finta is a personal finance tracker with no account to create, no cloud to sync to, and no company sitting between you and your own numbers. Everything lives in a single file on your device — and it budgets around your payday, not the 1st of the month.
one_email_when_it: One email when it ships. Nothing else, ever.
tap_a_day_to: Tap a day to see its transactions
your_budget_resets_on: Your budget resets on payday. Not on the 1st.
almost_every_finance_app: Almost every finance app slices your life into calendar months. If you get paid on the 25th, that split is wrong in a way that quietly ruins the numbers — your salary lands in one month while the rent, groceries and transport it pays for land in the next.
the_paycheque_is_already: The paycheque is already a week old when the window opens — so August shows a month of spending against almost no income.
the_window_opens_the: The window opens the day the money arrives and closes the day before the next one. One paycheque in, one paycheque's spending out.
set_your_payday_once: Set your payday once, during setup. From then on the entire app runs on that cycle — the dashboard, every budget, the analytics, the health score and the recap all use the same window.
pick_the_31st_and: Pick the 31st and February still works — the anchor clamps to the last day of short months instead of spilling into the next one.
periods_never_overlap_or: Periods never overlap or leave gaps.
each_one_ends_the: Each one ends the day before the next payday, whatever number you chose.
the_period_selector_sits: The period selector sits where the app title normally would, so last cycle is one tap away.
income_and_the_spending: Income and the spending it funds stay together
which_is_the_whole: , which is the whole reason savings rate and the health score mean anything.
there_is_no_server: There is no server to trust.
most_finance_apps_ask: Most finance apps ask you to hand over your spending history and then promise to look after it. Finta removes the step where you have to believe anyone. Your data never goes anywhere, because the app has nowhere to send it.
everything_is_a_single: Everything is a single SQLite database in the app's private storage. No copy exists anywhere else unless you make one yourself.
one_tap_on_the: One tap on the eye icon masks every number in the app at once — for handing your phone to someone, or just reading it on a crowded train.
back_up_to_a: Back up to a zip you keep, or export to CSV and open it in a spreadsheet. There is no lock-in to escape from.
no_tracking_is_easy: "No tracking" is easy to claim, so here is the version you can check yourself: turn on airplane mode and use Finta all day. Everything still works, because nothing was ever being sent anywhere. The app was built without the part that lets an app talk to the internet at all — so there is nothing quietly reporting what you tap, and nothing calling home when something goes wrong. There is also nothing to fetch an ad from: serving one means a network request, and that is the exact capability the app was built without. The insights, the unusual-spending warnings and the health score are sums and averages worked out on your phone. The only time your data moves is when you tap share on a backup or an export — and then it goes exactly where you send it.
it_notices_things_you: It notices things you never told it.
finta_reads_your_own: Finta reads your own history and points out what changed — without any of it leaving the phone.
when_the_same_merchant: When the same merchant charges you roughly the same amount roughly every month, Finta spots it and offers to start tracking it in one tap.
flags_an_unusual_amount: Flags an unusual amount as you type it.
if_a_coffee_costs: If a coffee costs ten times what your coffees normally cost, it asks before saving — and tells you what typical looks like. A nudge, never a block.
scores_your_financial_health: Scores your financial health out of 100
from_your_savings_rate: from your savings rate, how closely you hold your budgets, and how steady your income is — with all three sub-scores shown, not one mystery number.
before_it_becomes_a: before it becomes a surprise at the end of the cycle.
logging_a_transaction_takes: Logging a transaction takes three taps.
people_abandon_finance_trackers: People abandon finance trackers because entry is tedious. So entry is the part Finta works hardest on.
a_keypad_built_for: A keypad built for six-digit numbers,
key_because_typing_1: key — because typing 1.250.000 on a phone keyboard is how a habit dies.
do_maths_in_the: Do maths in the amount field.
and_it_just_works: and it just works. Splitting a bill needs no calculator app.
start_typing_a_place: Start typing a place you have been before and the account fills itself in.
for_the_things_you: for the things you buy constantly, plus duplicate, and bulk edit for when you catch up on a whole week at once.
85_used_means_nothing: "85% used" means nothing without a date.
being_85_through_your: Being 85% through your food budget is alarming on day 3 and completely fine on day 27. Every Finta budget bar carries a pace marker showing how far through the period you actually are, so the number has context.
switch_on_repeat_every: Switch on "Repeat every period" and the same limit comes back each cycle — monthly ones on your payday, not the 1st. Leave it off and it covers only the period you set it in.
pick_whether_a_quiet: Pick whether a quiet month tops up the next one, or whether overspending eats into it too.
you_get_told_at: You get told at 75% and again at 100%,
right_when_you_save: right when you save the transaction that crossed the line.
category_breakdowns_a_rolling: Category breakdowns, a rolling twelve-month cashflow, spend trends against your own average, a daily intensity calendar, and a ranking of the merchants quietly taking the most.
every_day_of_the: Every day of the cycle, shaded by how much went out. Tap any square to see that day.
the_rest_of_what: The rest of what's in there.
salary_rent_and_subscriptions: Salary, rent and subscriptions post themselves on schedule. Close the app for a month and everything catches up correctly when you open it.
set_a_target_put: Set a target, put money towards it, and see the date you'll actually get there based on how you've really been contributing.
money_you_lent_and: Money you lent and money you owe, with a payoff calculator that tells you how many months a given monthly payment needs.
cash_bank_credit_card: Cash, bank, credit card, e-wallet, savings and investment — with transfers between them and a running net worth. Cards show what you owe.
bring_in_a_csv: Bring in a CSV from your bank or another app, map the columns once, and preview it before anything is written.
each_pay_cycle_gets: Each pay cycle gets a summary card you can export as an image — and it waits until the period is actually finished before calling it a result.
both_languages_fully_translated: Both languages fully translated, not machine-filled. Rupiah is a first-class currency, formatted without decimals the way people actually write it.
a_warm_palette_designed: A warm palette designed to feel like a notebook rather than a trading terminal — including expenses in dusty rose instead of alarm red.
balances_and_goal_progress: Balances and goal progress are worked out from your transactions every time, so fixing an entry from three months ago fixes everything downstream.
does_it_connect_to: Does it connect to my bank?
no_and_that_is: No — and that is deliberate. Bank connections require handing your credentials to a third-party aggregator that then holds your full transaction history. Finta doesn't have a server, so it couldn't do that even if it wanted to. You enter transactions yourself, or import a CSV your bank already gives you.
do_i_have_to: Do I have to set my budgets up again every month?
only_if_you_want: Only if you want to. Every budget has a "Repeat every period" switch — turn it on and the same limit comes back each cycle, renewing on your payday rather than the 1st, carrying unspent money across if you asked for that. Leave it off and the budget covers just the period you made it in, then moves to an "Ended" list instead of disappearing. It is a switch rather than an assumption because a budget you deliberately chose to repeat is one you can still explain to yourself six months later.
what_happens_if_i: What happens if I lose my phone?
this_is_the_honest: This is the honest trade-off of a local-first app: if the only copy is on the phone and the phone is gone, the data is gone. Finta gives you a one-tap backup that produces a zip file you can put in your own cloud drive, email to yourself, or keep anywhere you like. Do it occasionally and you are covered — on your terms, in a file you control.
can_i_sync_between: Can I sync between two devices?
not_automatically_sync_means: Not automatically. Sync means a server, and a server means your spending history sits on someone else's computer — which is the exact thing this app is built to avoid. You can move data between devices with a backup file whenever you need to.
which_platforms_will_it: Which platforms will it be on?
android_and_ios_at: Android and iOS at launch. Join the waiting list and you'll hear once, on the day it's available.
pricing_isn_t_settled: Pricing isn't settled yet. What is settled: no ads, no analytics, and no selling data — none of which are possible in an app that doesn't make network requests.
can_i_get_my: Can I get my data out?
any_time_two_ways: Any time, two ways. A full backup is a zip containing the actual database file, and CSV export gives you a plain spreadsheet of every transaction. Both go straight to your share sheet.
track_your_money_not: Track your money, not your stress.
and_you_ll_get: and you'll get a single message the day it lands.
